newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela oilmin to demand OPEC reply over quotas.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela oilmin to demand OPEC reply over quotas.

text.p: Venezuelan Energy and Mines Minister Erwin Arrieta said on Thursday he would demand a reply from OPEC to the country's request for a change in the group's strategy towards world oil markets.

Ministers from the 11-member Organisation for Petroleum Exporting Countries are due to meet in Vienna next week to discuss their quota system, which limits the amount of crude oil supplied to the world market.
"Because OPEC has concentrated exclusively on quotas and prices, it has allowed others to occupy the space (in the market) that we are leaving empty," Arrieta told journalists in Congress.
"We are going to demand a reply to the working paper that we handed over in June last year with regard to a change in the strategy and policy towards the market."
He echoed comments by Venezuela's state oil company president Luis Giusti earlier this week, who called for the cartel to scrap its quota system altogether in favour of a push for market share.
Venezuela is OPEC's biggest quota violator, with current output running about 900,000 bpd above its official quota of 2.359 million.
The country is also going through a radical liberalisation of its state-run oil industry, attracting foreign companies back to help it double its current production within 10 years.
